title: Cincinnati chilli
subtitle: Ohio's Greek-American spiced meat sauce over spaghetti
excerpt: A cinnamon-and-allspice-spiced beef sauce with Mediterranean aromatics, served over spaghetti and topped with finely shredded cheddar. Ohio's distinctive chilli style, originally developed by Greek immigrants in the 1920s.
sourceNotes: Cincinnati chilli was developed in the 1920s by Macedonian immigrants, most notably Tom Kiradjieff, who opened Empress Chili in Cincinnati in 1922. The dish reflects a Mediterranean spice profile applied to American beef. It is documented in multiple American regional cooking books and is a recognised regional cuisine of Ohio. Served as 2-way (pasta + chilli), 3-way (+ cheddar), 4-way (+ beans or onion), or 5-way (+ both).

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the chilli sauce alone. Defrost and reheat; cook fresh pasta to serve.
recipe.batchNotes: The sauce doubles well and is even better after a day in the fridge.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the sauce up to 3 days ahead. Improves with time.

content.text: Cincinnati chilli is not like Texas chilli. There are no dried chilli peppers, no chipotles, no heat. Instead: cinnamon, allspice, bay leaves, and a small amount of chilli powder for colour and mild warmth. The beef is simmered in water (not browned first), which gives the sauce its distinctive thin-but-rich texture. It is served over spaghetti, which makes it one of the most divisive dishes in American food culture and one of the most compelling.

items.prepNote: finely shredded (use the fine side of a box grater)

content.text: Put the beef mince into a large saucepan with 250 ml water. Break it up and cook over medium heat, stirring, until the meat loses its pink colour and is in fine crumbles. Do not brown it. Pour off most of the fat.

Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes. Add the tomato paste and all the spices. Stir for 1 minute. Add the stock, tomatoes, vinegar, and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer and cook, uncovered, for 60 to 70 minutes until the sauce has reduced and is no longer watery. Remove the bay leaves. Taste and season.

Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water and drain. Serve the spaghetti in mounds in shallow bowls. Ladle the chilli over the top. Heap with finely shredded cheddar. This is the classic 3-way; a 5-way adds kidney beans and chopped raw onion.

items.symptom: Sauce is too thin after 70 minutes
items.cause: Too much liquid; meat released a lot of water
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for another 15 minutes. Cincinnati chilli should be thin compared to Texas chilli, but not watery.

content.text: Cincinnati chilli is the defining regional dish of the Ohio River Valley. Empress Chili opened in 1922 and Skyline Chili followed in 1949. Between them they created a food culture built around parlours dedicated exclusively to this one dish. The cinnamon and Mediterranean spice profile reflects the Greek and Macedonian heritage of the founders. It is categorically unlike Texan or New Mexican chilli. Cincinnatians eat approximately two million pounds of it a year, which should settle the debate about whether it is good.
